**Apex Foods & Beverages - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript**

**Operator:**  
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Foods & Beverages Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):**  
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Foods & Beverages' Q3 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Growth Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

**Mike Thompson (CEO):**  
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: performance in key channels including retail, foodservice, and convenience; gross margin analysis covering drivers and trends; our revised full-year guidance; and capital expenditure plans and priorities.

First, regarding performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience. These core segments, making up over 95% of revenues, posted aggregate organic net sales growth of 6.2%, with balanced contributions from volume and pricing, marking six straight quarters of volume gains ahead of the broader industry.

Second, concerning gross margin analysis: drivers and trends. We expanded margins to 42.5%, up 230 basis points year-over-year, thanks to pricing discipline, favorable mix, and efficiency gains outpacing input cost pressures.

Third, in terms of revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance. We're raising our outlook across key metrics, reflecting robust Q3 momentum and productivity levers.

Finally, looking at capital expenditure plans and priorities. We're planning measured investments around $1.4 to $1.5 billion next year to fuel capacity, resilience, and innovation.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

**Lisa Chen (CFO):**  
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3. Net sales were $7.8 billion, representing a 6.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, benefiting from pricing actions and mix shifts despite some commodity headwinds. Operating income was $850 million, and earnings per share were $1.15. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $2.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and $1.2 billion in share repurchases this year.

To give you a deeper view, let me expand on those four areas Mike highlighted, starting with our performance across the key channels of retail, foodservice, and convenience, which drive over 95% of our net revenues. In Q3, these delivered combined organic net sales growth of 6.2%, split evenly between 3.1% volume increases and 3.1% from price and mix. This extends our streak to six consecutive quarters of positive volume, surpassing the overall food and beverage category's 2.8% growth according to IRI and Nielsen metrics.

Diving channel by channel, retail—our biggest at 58% of sales—led with 8.4% organic growth, the best since late 2021. Volumes rose 4.2% on lingering at-home consumption, matched by price/mix from core pricing and premium shifts. In North America, 65% of retail, we grabbed 110 basis points of share in the $150 billion grocery space to hit 14.2% overall per Nielsen. Brands like Apex Pure Juices and Harvest Bites snacks boosted household penetration by 2.3% through 2,500 added ACV points at Walmart and Kroger. Low-sugar versions saw 7% higher velocity, riding health trends like appetite suppressants favoring nutrient-rich choices.

EMEA grew 7.1%, shining in the UK and Germany where plant-based dairy alternatives surged 15% with EU Green Deal support. APAC eased to 5.8% on China's slowdown but countered with 12% in India via localized Heritage Snacks at 1,200 new Reliance Retail doors. We're pushing Digital Shelf 2.0 with AI planograms from Trax and Crisp, lifting on-shelf availability to 96% for a 3-point impulse boost. We've trimmed 15% of low-velocity SKUs to back functional beverages like zero-sugar Apex Surge in the $25 billion energy market.

Foodservice, 28% of sales, grew 4.7% organically. Volumes up 2.8% as QSR traffic hit 95% of pre-pandemic per Black Box Intelligence, with price/mix at 1.9%. North America paced at 5.5%, powered by our McDonald's renewal for Apex Fruit Blends across 14,000 sites, adding 200 basis points. QSR ACV reached 62%, with Yum! Brands same-store sales up 6% on spicy sauces. Casual dining grew slower at 2.1% amid labor gaps—U.S. restaurant participation still 4% below 2019 per NRA. Latin America hit 6.2% despite Brazil's flu issues via diversified proteins at Pollo Campero. EMEA at 3.4% balanced quick-casual like Pret A Manger against Germany's 18% logistics hikes.

Initiatives like Precision Forecasting with Blue Yonder cut QSR stockouts 25%, and we're at 80% cage-free eggs by year-end for Starbucks and Chipotle compliance. FY24 target is 7-9% growth via ghost kitchens and DoorDash kits, where penetration rises 20% yearly.

Convenience, 14% of sales, topped with 7.9% growth—3.7% volume, 4.2% price/mix—and holds 15% U.S. C-store share in the $65 billion market per Technomic. North America at 9.2% via Circle K and 7-Eleven single-serve Apex Energy Shots with 22% velocity on 24/7 snacking. Fuel forecourt up 12% as prices steadied, lifting average baskets to $4.50. APAC glowed at 8.5% with Japan's Lawson matcha drinks at 30% more distribution in the $10 billion konbini space. EMEA at 4.1% despite UK tobacco rules.

C-Store Connect app syncs inventory with POS for 98% fill rates on short-shelf-life items, and we're piloting EV chargers at Buc-ee's for the $50 billion shift by 2030.

Geographically, North America grew 7.1%, EMEA 5.3%, APAC 6.8%, LatAm 5.9%, with emerging markets now 28% of sales versus 24% two years back. Premium health SKUs drove 60% of gains; innovation pipeline is 70% RTD beverages and clean snacks like Celsius and Kind models. Inflation eased to 2% on commodities but packaging up 5%—hedged 80% of 2024, PepsiCo-style supplier pacts for recycled PET. Value plays include club packs and B2B bundles. Q4 eyes 5-7% channel growth, full-year organic sales 6.5%, with retail leading, foodservice rebounding, convenience at 28% EBITDA flow-through.

Shifting to gross margin analysis, we hit 42.5% consolidated, up 230 basis points year-over-year from 40.2% and 110 sequentially from Q2's 41.4%. Third straight quarter of gains, trailing four-quarter average at 41.8%—above our 40% target and peers like Mondelez and General Mills in the mid-38s.

Volume, mix, and price drove 65% of the YoY lift. Pricing added 320 basis points via 6-8% hikes on snacks, beverages, plant-based dairy—no volume loss due to premium equity in Organic Harvest snacks and NitroBrew coffees. Consumers uptrade in inflation at 4.2% category-wide per Nielsen; EDLP on yogurts held 1.2 North America share points.

COGS fell 90 basis points to 57.5% from mix (premium/keto bars, almond milks up 15% at 48-50% margins vs. 38% legacy) and efficiencies—McKinsey notes premium outgrowing staples 2x. Input inflation hit 150 basis points: cocoa +22% on El Niño West Africa shortfalls like Hershey's woes, coffee +12% Brazil, oils +8% Indonesia palm, wheat/dairy milder at 3-5% via 70% FY24 hedging 10% below spot. FX aided 20 basis points on strong USD for EU imports.

North America (55% revenue) up 280 to 44.2% on post-strike resets and Ohio automation saving $15 million yearly via robotics/AI throughput +18%. Europe (25%) +150 to 39.8%, offset by EU deforestation on cocoa but edged Nestlé with Fair Trade. Emerging (20%) +200 to 41.1% on local India co-ops cutting logistics 12%, Brazil FX shield.

Tech like SAP S/4HANA at 80% plants forecasts COGS 95% accurately, saving $8 million. $200 million soybean plant acquisition locks 40% non-GMO at -15%. Regenerative cocoa in Côte d'Ivoire for 5-7% savings/ESG pricing.

Q4 margins 42.7-43.3%, FY24 42.0% +180 basis points. Cocoa risk to $4,500/tonne countered by $500 million hedges/dynamic pricing. Path to 44% FY26.

Next, our revised full-year guidance, which we're raising on Q3 strength—organic sales +7.2% with 4.8% volume, 2.4% pricing; adjusted op income +11% to $285 million, margins +140 to 22.4%. Core brands like FrostPeak sodas, PureHarvest juices, VitalFlow functionals shine.

FY24 organic sales now 5-6% vs. prior 3-5%: 3.5% volume on health demand, 1.5-2.5% pricing vs. sugar/aluminum/PET via 85% Q1 hedges. Adjusted EPS $4.25-4.45 from $4.00-4.20, +$0.35 midpoint on $175 million productivity—12% over 2023 via AgriYield 2.0: IBM Watson logistics -8% North America, Brazil orange precision +15% despite El Niño.

Gross margins +100-150 to 38.5-39.0% on savings/mix; VitalFlow 18% beverages (from 12%), double-digit on zero-sugar/adaptogens in $25 billion market.

North America (65%) 6-7% on QSR fountain +12% McDonald's/Taco Bell, e-com 15% Amazon/Instacart, +2.2 energy share. EMEA (20%) 4-5% vs. 2-4% on yogurt pricing vs. 5% dairy, GreenLeaf plant-based +20% UK/Germany Farm-to-Fork. APAC/LatAm (15%) 7-8% vs. 5-7%: China tea JV +25%, Mexico +10% pricing, Brazil hydration.

Pillars: premiumization to 60% portfolio by 2026, sustainability Scope 3 -18% YTD Driscoll's regen, digital OmniChannel 50k outlets -12 inventory days. Risks: cocoa +40%, <3% mix; value slowdowns offset by snacking data. Outperform peers in growth/EPS, $1.2 billion buybacks, 2.8% yield.

Finally, capital expenditure plans. FY24 $1.25 billion or 4.2% of $29.8 billion TTM revenue, +12% from 2023, balancing capacity/resilience vs. mid-single digit commodity easing.

FY25 $1.4-1.5 billion or 4.5-4.8% of $32-33 billion sales, +12-20%, high-ROI <3.5 year paybacks, ROIC >8.2% WACC. Stress-tested vs. +10% costs/Panama-like droughts.

Buckets: 40% (~$560-600 million) manufacturing—$250 million Modesto aseptic lines +25% plant-based like NutriPlant Oat Milk vs. Oatly/Chobani $15 billion alt-dairy. NA 45%, APAC Vietnam greenfield RTD teas 20% growth, Europe RTE EU regs, EM spices.

25% (~$350-375 million) supply chain—$200 million RPA/AGVs 15-20% throughput like Nestlé, Chicago ABB pilot, $80 million cold-chain vs. $25 billion spoilage. EMEA Poland nearshoring Red Sea, LatAm El Niño warehouses.

20% (~$280-300 million) ESG—$150 million regen/energy biomass -25% Scope 1 by 2027, $75 million water recycling +40 million gallons -18%, $55 million rPET 50% by 2028 EU bans. APAC/EM water stress drip-irrigation.

15% (~$210-225 million) digital/R&D—$120 million AI SAP/digital twins R&D -33% cycles, SKU prune 15% of 5,000 to zero-sugar +22%.

Projections: +$400 million EBITDA by 2027, 2.5x IRR. 85% ops-funded, debt 4.2% net debt/EBITDA 2.1x. Hedged 70% inputs. Outgrow Kraft Heinz/Kellogg CapEx, 8-10% organic, Net Zero 2040.

For the full year, we are raising our guidance for organic sales growth to 5-6%, adjusted EPS to $4.25-$4.45, and gross margins to 42%.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

**Operator:**  
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

**John Smith (Goldman Sachs):**  
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

**Mike Thompson (CEO):**  
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a key focus, but our strategies have insulated us well. We've realized 6-8% pricing across core categories without eroding volumes, leveraging brand strength in premiums like Organic Harvest and NitroBrew. Input costs pressured by 150 basis points—cocoa up 22% on poor harvests, coffee 12%, oils 8%—but hedging 70-85% of FY24/25 needs at below-spot rates has de-risked much of it. Packaging rose 5%, offset by supplier collaborations for recycled materials akin to PepsiCo-Amcor deals. Regionally, North America's automation and local sourcing in emerging markets cut logistics 12%. Consumer trading up to value-added helped, with Nielsen showing category inflation at 4.2%. Our productivity via AI forecasting and AgriYield saved $175 million, flowing to margins. We're positioned to handle persistence, with dynamic pricing algorithms ready.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

**Emily Davis (Morgan Stanley):**  
What are your plans for new products and what is the expected impact?

**Raj Patel (Chief Growth Officer):**  
Thanks, Emily. Innovation is central, with 70% of our pipeline in RTD beverages and clean-label snacks. Key launches include zero-sugar Apex Surge energy drinks targeting Red Bull/Monster gaps in the $25 billion segment, and VitalFlow adaptogen-infused functionals now 18% of beverages, up from 12%, with double-digit growth on health trends. Low-sugar reformulations in PureHarvest juices and Harvest Bites drove 7-22% velocity lifts. Plant-based dairy like NutriPlant Oat Milk expands via new aseptic lines +25% capacity for $15 billion alt-dairy share. Localized like Masala Chai yogurts and matcha RTD in APAC. Impact: these premium/health SKUs fueled 60% of channel growth, 15% YoY category surge, boosting mix 4% and margins to 48-50%. E-com and C-store pilots like Energy Shots add impulse. Expect 3.5% volume tailwind FY24, positioning for 8-10% organic long-term.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Tom Wilson with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

**Tom Wilson (JPMorgan):**  
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

**Elena Vargas (Chief Supply Chain Officer):**  
Hi Tom. Disruptions like port strikes, Red Sea issues, avian flu, and El Niño persist, but our investments yield resilience. Precision Forecasting with Blue Yonder/ML cut QSR stockouts 25%, fill rates to 98% in C-stores via C-Store Connect POS integration. RPA/AGVs at 15 plants boost throughput 15-20%, $15 million Ohio savings. Nearshoring Poland facility bypasses spice import risks, Vietnam greenfield doubles APAC RTD. Hedging 80% commodities, local co-ops India/Brazil -12% logistics. SAP S/4HANA real-time COGS 95% accurate, OmniChannel 50k outlets -12 inventory days. Cold-chain upgrades, climate warehouses vs. spoilage/$25 billion industry loss. Digital twins predict swings 90 days out. Post-Panama drought lessons stress-tested CapEx. Result: on-shelf 96%, turnover for perishables, emerging markets from 24% to 28% sales with diversified proteins.

**Operator:**  
Our last question comes from Laura Chen with Barclays. Please proceed.

**Laura Chen (Barclays):**  
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

**Lisa Chen (CFO):**  
Thanks, Laura. Q4 channels guide 5-7% growth, full-year organic 6.5%, led by retail 8%+, foodservice 7-9% traffic rebound, convenience margin resilience. Gross margins 42.7-43.3% Q4, FY24 42.0% +180 bps. Sales 5-6%, EPS $4.25-4.45 on $175 million savings. North America 6-7%, EMEA 4-5%, APAC/LatAm 7-8%. Risks like cocoa to $4,500/tonne buffered by $500 million hedges, but tailwinds from premiumization 60% portfolio, sustainability -18% Scope 3, digital efficiencies. Productivity, away-from-home recovery, e-com 15%, health demand sustain momentum. Confident in execution, outperforming peers.

**Operator:**  
I would now like to turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

**Mike Thompson (CEO):**  
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in Apex Foods & Beverages. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

**Operator:**  
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
